issues.description: validate_conda silently swallows decode failures and only checks substring match
issues.detail: The validator decodes subprocess output with default encoding and checks if any of ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"] appears as a substring. Note that "mamba" is a substring of "micromamba", and "conda" appears in many unrelated strings (e.g., "anaconda", "second"). The data shape here is wrong: the right structure is the parsed `--version` first token, not a substring scan. Also: bare `except Exception` after a single `communicate()` hides real problems (missing decode codec, non-zero exit). Strip the cleverness, parse the first whitespace token, compare equality.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' is wrong shape for a cross-platform path
issues.detail: Conda executables on macOS/Linux have no extension; on Windows the wrapper is typically `conda.bat` or `conda.exe`. Hardcoding `*.exe` as the file dialog filter is platform-specific data masquerading as universal config. The right data structure is a per-platform filter (or no filter at all); the algorithm — file picking — then becomes obvious and correct on every OS.

issues.description: Config lookup chain in argv() is harder to read than the data it represents
issues.detail: The fallback chain in `argv()` nests a ternary inside an assignment inside an `if not conda_exe`. The data is simple: 'custom path if enabled, else None'. Pull it into two lines — `custom_enabled = self.get_conf(...)` and `conda_exe = self.get_conf('conda_path', ...) if custom_enabled else None` — before the outer guard. Same behavior, obvious shape.

issues.description: Empty string sentinel doubles as 'valid' in validate_conda
issues.detail: `validate_conda("")` returns True. That's a UI convenience (don't flag the field red when blank) leaking into a function whose name promises validation of an executable. Either rename to `is_acceptable_conda_field` or push the empty-string special-case into the caller. Small, but the data structure (a Maybe[Path]) would make this self-evident.

The textbox value is fed directly to `os.path.isfile` and `os.access`. A trailing space, surrounding quotes (common on Windows when users paste from Properties), or `~` won't expand. A two-line `os.path.expanduser(path.strip().strip('"'))` would make the validator robust without any algorithmic cleverness — the right data shape removes the failure modes.

issues.description: edit.setFocus() side effect added to a generic file-picker helper
issues.detail: `select_file` is shared infrastructure; tacking on `edit.setFocus()` to fix one screen's behavior changes the contract for every caller of `create_browsefile`. If focus-after-pick is wanted for the conda field specifically, wire it where the conda field is created. Small composable tools shouldn't grow side effects for one caller's convenience.

review.summary: The feature is small and the data flow is sensible: a checkbox plus a path, persisted to config, consulted in `argv()` as a fallback when auto-discovery fails. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE in shape. The concrete weakness is `validate_conda` — WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE for what it claims to do: substring matching on decoded `--version` output, bare-except swallowing failures, no path normalization, and an empty-string-is-valid sentinel that conflates UI state with validation. The `*.exe` filter is Windows-only logic in a cross-platform code path. The `argv()` fallback chain is fine but reads better as two lines than as a nested ternary, and `select_file` shouldn't grow `setFocus()` side effects for one caller. None of these are blockers, but the validator and the file filter are worth fixing before merge.
